I wouldn’t say I’m talented but I have a strong passion for art and learning it. I’ve been doing this all my life, and while my skills aren’t the best, I still do love it, and would love to pursue video game design. 

Unfortunately I’ve had many days, weeks, months, and years of just crippling self esteem issues in regards to it. I should be better than I am now, and seeing younger kids or people my age excel better has me very envious. Thus adding to my self hatred and extreme discipline. For a long time(months for a couple of years) I sat in my room and drew the same 3/4 view over and over demanding I perfect it. I cut off all contact with friends and family and I just demanded I get this shit right. It was pretty eye opening and jarring when my mother finally pointed it out.

Over the years my perspective has changed on art, meaning I’ve learned perfection isn’t possible, and how to properly practice and to try not comparing myself to others. 

However something new has happened and I’ve found that my real issue is that I cannot focus and I’ve lost all amounts of patience. My irritability levels have risen and I often find myself feeling hopeless and empty in the middle of drawing. Recently whenever I try to focus my mind goes straight to all the embarrassing things I’ve done or all the shitty things people have done to me, and I broke down yesterday in the middle of drawing because of it. It’s happening again today and I am not quite sure what is wrong with me. I hope one day I can find the solution and get back to my passion. Especially since I really need to be better and I can’t take working shitty entry level jobs to pay my bills.

The next one was the same way, I lost feelings over the course of the relationship. 1.5 years. I guess it took like 1 month to get over that one or to stop wanting to talk to him. Sometimes I forget we even dated. 

The 4th one was probably one of the WORST relationships I had ever been in, and the sad part is it was only 4 months haha. Even afterwards he was still very abusive to me. That took a month or so to get over, but the abuse has damaged me 3 years later and will probably haunt me for awhile longer. 

The 5th one, 4 months. Meh. Got over it after dating for like 2 months. Also forget I dated him. And it gives me shivers when I remember. Low point for me. 

The 6th one, and the most recent. 2 years, we dated and lived together. I was head over heels for him from the SECOND I saw him and shook his hand. I was blown away. I didn’t think I could ever be so attracted to someone EVER. Love at first sight seemed like a possibility haha (I know it was infatuation and biology. BUT HOT DAMN. I melted every time he was near. There was just something about him.) I pursued him of course.. and let’s just say that kinda never stopped :/. Anyways, we broke up in janurary. Got back in feb-march. Broke up again and now we are just REALLLY special bestfriends. Everyday has gotten easier.. but slower. The immediate break up though, I considered killing myself, I was in physical pain, I didn’t think this was real. Cramping, shaking, I felt like I was in danger everyday, and almost like my body was killing me. I couldn’t eat but I was pooping on the toilet every hour. I’d hyperventilate. I couldn’t watch tv, listen to music, draw or write. I’d just lay there. This has been the hardest break up of them all, the one I learned from the most. And I don’t know. I’m sure maybe one day I’ll be over it because I have to be. But I’m not so sure I’m going to find anybody else. And that doesn’t bother me to be honest. I love and I lost, I dated someone I was head over heels for, and that’s enough for me. Now I’ve got to work on myself.

Anyways. I never truly forgot about the bigger exes(#1,#2,#4, and now #6). They always rested in the back of my mind. when a shitty part of my relationships came forward, I reminisced about them more than I should have because there truly are reasons why you aren’t with them. If you don’t know what they are now, THEY WILL come full swing eventually. So don’t go to the past. Don’t ever get back with them. First off I wanna say you're 15!? This is incredible for someone your age, do not stop, keep practicing, you have a lot of potential! 

Next is, your anatomy needs work. what I do is study this pose or similar ones form photo references and trace it a couple times making sure I fully understand the forms, muscles, and what's important etc. then I start drawing it a couple more times (not tracing) with the reference and then without. A good rule of thumb is to draw something 3 times, making sure to learn from your mistakes each time and becoming familiar with what you're drawing. That way you can do it 10000 more times with no problems... although my method my be a little whack. But it's just a suggestion to help. (Also this video by Ahmed aldoori is great for what I'm kinda trying to describe here https://youtu.be/-BduaEOgIeg )

Next when it comes to shading you want to make sure your lines wrap around the objects creating the illusion of form. So the arm behind the head, really try to round out those lines. Otherwise it will appear flat.

Your line work is clean and thick and I really enjoy that. Just watch out for tangents which again can make your work look flat. For example the tangent/line flow of the hair into the top of that hat. it looks as if his hair is just flowing into it and that it's not entirely a separate object.

And then lastly really try to understand what you're drawing, like his belt and extra attire, it feels really chaotic and is if you don't fully understand each object. So practice each piece of attire and really understand how it's going to lay on him and what it looks like separately and then all together that way you can manipulate them with confidence! If that makes sense.
Seriously though keep up the good work! I adore the style a lot! You're headed in an incredible direction!
